For the first time in 80 years, the federal debt-to-GDP ratio is over 100%. 

In the past, the rich used to pay higher taxes.  

Now, the government pays the rich interest on a swelling debt, caused largely by lower taxes on the rich. 

It's a big switcheroo. Watch.

Video

Instead of spending $50 billion to bankroll Trump’s criminal war on Iran, we could:

-Extend ACA subsidies for one year
-Restore SNAP benefits for 2.4 million people
-And ensure Medicaid coverage for nearly 2 million people

It’s not about what we can afford. It’s about priorities.

Political corruption is even worse than you think.

To build a functioning one-person-one-vote system where oligarchs don’t pull the strings, we need to make anti-corruption the central focus of our politics.

@davidsirota explains why.

Video

"Freedom is not a state; it is an act. It is not some enchanted garden perched high on a distant plateau where we can finally sit down and rest. Freedom is the continuous action we all must take, and each generation must do its part to create an even more fair, more just society." —John Lewis

The Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act of 1965 this week.

It was a slap in the face to the countless activists who fought for the VRA — and those who died for it.

But we cannot give up. Here's how we should respond.

But remember: We outnumber the oligarchs.

The world’s ten richest people — all Americans — saw their collective net worth increase by $260 billion in April.

These ten people are now worth a combined $2.7 trillion.

The bottom 50% of U.S. households, 66 million in total, is worth $4.3 trillion. 

Wondering if inequality is out of control?

As Trump's Iran War drags on, the Pentagon has agreed to buy interceptor drones from Powerus — a company backed by Trump's sons Eric and Don Jr.

Trump used to rail against the military industrial complex. Now his family profits from it.

Google co-founder Sergey Brin — the third-richest man on the planet — is reportedly spending $57M to defeat California's proposed billionaire's tax. 

So he and his fellow oligarchs can't afford a wealth tax, but they'll spend a fortune buying elections?

See the problem...

"Call it democracy, or call it democratic socialism, but there must be a better distribution of wealth within this country for all God's children." 

—MLK Jr.
If you want to understand why our economy is rigged for the super rich, look at this graph.

More accurate estimates found that Trump’s war on Iran has cost $50B.

That money would fund a year of the ACA subsidies that he and the GOP have refused to extend — with $20B left over.

Instead, millions of Americans have dropped their insurance because they can’t afford it.

Priorities.

Reminder that Amazon...

-Helps fuel ICE's deportation machine

-Donated $1M to Trump's inauguration

-Scrapped plans to display tariff costs after pressure from Trump

-Shelled out $75M for the Melania movie

And now wants to reboot The Apprentice — with Don Jr as host.

Still shopping on Amazon?

Today, May Day, is the Workers Over Billionaires national day of action! March, rally & take direct action at 1 of the over 4000 events across the country today! 

Find an action near you at maydaystrong.org!

Trump feigns strength, but he's operating from a place of weakness.

Remember this.

Due to Trump's big ugly bill, the richest New Yorkers will collectively get a $12B federal tax cut in 2026. Meanwhile, over 1 million New Yorkers could lose healthcare and SNAP benefits.

Gov. Hochul & other states can fight Trump's trickle down scam by taxing the rich — who will still be rich.

Never forget this: Working people outnumber the billionaires and CEOs by a huge margin.

When workers stand together, they win.

Solidarity. #MayDay

The Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act of 1965 this week. It was a slap in the face to the countless activists who fought for the VRA — and those who died for it. But we cannot give up. Here's how we should respond.
You've probably heard a lot about general strikes. But how exactly do they work? And is America on the verge of one? Labor journalist Kim Kelly explains.
The decision made today by the Supreme Court’s conservative majority was dishonest and shameful. I want to share some thoughts on what it means — and how we move forward.

A Supreme Court so fundamentally hostile to the rights of minority voters places the Court at odds with democracy itself. This is the legacy of Chief Justice John Roberts. I opposed his nomination back in 2005, and I stand by that.
An actual king understands democracy better than Trump.

Donald Trump wants you to think that the least powerful people in this country are the most responsible for your problems. But you can’t deport your way out of a rigged economy. Former FTC Commissioner Alvaro Bedoya explains how economic populism can bring workers of all stripes together — and is the only real antidote to Trumpism.
We must make anti-corruption the central focus of our politics. David Sirota of The Lever shares three ways to do that.
The affordability crisis isn’t an accident — it’s driven by concentrated corporate power. Just look at the latest evidence in California's price-fixing case against Amazon.
I don't buy Tucker Carlson's apology for boosting Trump. No one else should either. Let me explain what's really going on.
If you don’t think Donald Trump has completely lost his marbles, then you need to watch this.
